audit.name: Cordage
audit.ageGap: Root node; no prerequisite.

effectsProposed.why: Nets, snares and lines let each forager-fisher take more fish and small game per year.

audit.costConcern: 1,050 is high for an A1 root next to basketry 620 and shelter_hut 260, but it is a hub that unlocks most of A1-A2; acceptable.
audit.rationale: Correct root: fibre twisting has no technical precursor beyond hands and plants. Hub node with 11 dependents; keep.

audit.name: Basketry

prereqAssessment.why: Coiled and twined basketry uses the same twisting and binding of fibre that cordage establishes.

audit.ageGap: A1 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: Baskets let households cache nuts, seeds and dried fish, so a lean season is partly absorbed from store.

audit.rationale: Causal prerequisite is right. The live unlock (infra.fish_weir) is its main effect; a small storage effect gives the container role its own weight.

audit.name: Framed hut

prereqAssessment.why: Framed huts are lashed together; without cordage there is no frame of poles or bones.

audit.ageGap: A1 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: A lashed frame with a turf or hide cover outlasts a windbreak, so dwellings survive more seasons.

audit.costConcern: 260 is the cheapest node in the group; fine for a single-prerequisite A1 step.
audit.rationale: Minimal and correct prerequisite; the frame is the bridge to timber_frame.

audit.name: Hide working

prereqAssessment.why: Hide scrapers are prepared-core flake tools; the Middle Palaeolithic scraper kit is what makes systematic hide work possible.

audit.ageGap: A1 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: Scraped and softened hides make clothing and covers that cut exposure deaths in cold seasons.

audit.rationale: Correct causal prerequisite (cross-lane to materials, same Age).

audit.name: Eyed needle and sewing

prereqAssessment.why: Fitted garments are sewn from prepared hides and furs.
Sewing needs thread or sinew twisted into cord.

audit.ageGap: A1 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: Tailored, sewn clothing and tents let people cross and settle cold country, so migrants travel further.

audit.costConcern: 260 is cheap for a two-prerequisite node; fine for A1.
audit.rationale: AND is right: both the material (hide) and the thread are required. The node is the cold-climate expansion enabler, so its effect is on migration reach.

audit.name: Wool sheep and fleece

prereqAssessment.why: Woolly fleece is a product of selective breeding of domestic sheep.
Weak but harmless: fleece was selected because fibre could already be twisted into yarn; it keeps the fibre logic of the lane.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A1, A2.

effectsProposed.why: Fleece is a second, annual product from the same flock, so each herder yields more.

audit.rationale: Keep: the sheep_goat atom is essential; cordage is weak but not wrong and removing it would change nothing material.

audit.name: Mudbrick
audit.ageGap: Root node; no prerequisite.

effectsProposed.why: Earth walls replace timber walls, so a dwelling needs less timber.

audit.rationale: Root is defensible: moulded earth bricks need no prior technique in the tree. The live unlock (building.city_wall) is kept; the timber saving is its housing role.

audit.name: Lime plaster

prereqAssessment.why: Quicklime is made by burning limestone at ~800 C; controlled fire is the causal precursor.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: Plastered walls and floors shed rain and damp, so earth and stone houses last longer.
Plastered bins and floors keep stored grain dry and away from rodents.

audit.rationale: Correct, minimal causal prerequisite (cross-lane to energy, A1 to A2).

audit.name: Timber-frame construction

prereqAssessment.why: Ground stone axes and adzes fell and shape the posts and beams.
The framed hut is the direct structural ancestor of the post-and-beam house.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: Post-and-beam longhouses roof large spaces, so one dwelling houses a larger household.

audit.rationale: Correct AND. After the loom change it still has four dependents (canal_lock, track_road, traction_trebuchet, well).

audit.name: Dry-stone construction

prereqAssessment.why: Pecked and ground stone working is the precursor of fitted unmortared stone.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A1.

effectsProposed.why: Stone footings and walls rot no timber, so less timber goes into yearly repair.

audit.rationale: Correct. Hub for walls, harbour and built roads (all live).

audit.name: Dug well

prereqAssessment.why: Stone-lined shafts (Atlit-Yam) are one way to keep a well open.
Timber-lined shafts (LBK oak wells) are the other.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A2.

effectsProposed.why: Groundwater from a lined shaft is cleaner and steadier than pond or stream water.

audit.rationale: OR is right: either lining technique suffices.

audit.name: Spindle spinning
audit.prereq: cordage AND (flax OR wool OR cotton_cultivation)

prereqAssessment.why: The spindle mechanises the twisting that cordage does by hand.
One of three alternative fibre sources; OR is right.
Alternative fibre source; OR is right.
Alternative fibre source; OR is right.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A1, A2.

effectsProposed.why: Spun thread at volume makes woven sacks and bags, so grain and other bulk goods are packed and hauled more cheaply.

audit.rationale: cordage AND (any fibre) is the right shape: any one spinnable fibre suffices.

audit.name: Warp-weighted loom

prereqAssessment.why: A loom needs spun thread for the warp.

A warp-weighted loom is two uprights and a beam leaned on a wall; it does not need post-and-beam house joinery. Chronology also fails: Çatalhöyük textiles (~7,000 BCE) predate LBK timber framing (~5,500 BCE).

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A2. After the change its only prerequisite is A2, same Age.

effectsProposed.why: Cloth production supports specialist weavers and workshops, so a larger specialist class can exist.

audit.costConcern: 2,090 is high against A2 peers (440-1,760); expect the per-(tree, Age) calibration to bring it down.
audit.rationale: Remove timber_frame: not causal, and dated 1,500 years after the node's own emerged date (contract §6 chronology). The textile workshop it requires (inst.textile_workshop) is not live, so the node gets a specialist-class effect.

audit.name: Dyeing

prereqAssessment.why: Dye is applied to fibre and thread; spun fibre is what is dyed.
Mineral pigment preparation is the precursor of dye and mordant chemistry.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A1, A2.

effectsProposed.why: Coloured cloth and dyestuffs are high-value trade goods, so merchants close price gaps between places faster.

audit.rationale: Correct AND; A1 ochre to A2 dyeing is a reasonable cross-Age chain.

audit.name: Basin irrigation

prereqAssessment.why: Floodplain basins were built for cereal fields.
Alternative cultivated base; OR is right.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A2.

effectsProposed.why: Bunded basins hold the flood in place, so harvests track the flood less erratically.

audit.costConcern: 440 is low next to irrigation_canal 1,760; the gap is plausible (bunding is simpler than levelled channels).
audit.rationale: OR over staple crops is right.

audit.name: Canal irrigation

prereqAssessment.why: Canal irrigation served cereal fields.
Alternative cultivated base; OR is right.

audit.ageGap: A2 node; prerequisites from A2.
audit.crossTree: Civic dependents: water_rights. Dependent water_rights is a civic.

effectsProposed.why: Water led beyond the rainfall line makes each cultivated square kilometre yield more.

audit.rationale: OR over staples is right; surveying (A3) is not required for the Samarran canals.

audit.name: Ashlar fortification

prereqAssessment.why: Cut-stone walls are ashlar work.
Laying out curtain walls, towers and gate approaches needs measured layout.

audit.ageGap: A4 node; prerequisites from A3.

effectsProposed.why: Garrisoned stone strongholds hold distant districts, so administrative reach decays more slowly.

audit.rationale: Correct. Its live unlocks are AND/OR with other nodes (castle also needs vault_dome; lighthouse is already open via ashlar), so a reach effect gives it its own weight.

audit.name: Qanat

prereqAssessment.why: The mother well and access shafts are dug wells.
The gradient of a qanat (often <1:1000) needs levelling.
Underground tunnelling between shafts is mining technique.

audit.ageGap: A4 node; prerequisites from A2, A3.

effectsProposed.why: Aquifer water reaches arid plains without evaporation, raising yields where rain alone fails.

audit.rationale: Correct three-way AND. Deliberate leaf.

audit.name: Rock-cut water tunnel

prereqAssessment.why: Rock-cut tunnels are mining technique applied to water.
Eupalinos's tunnel was dug from both ends and met; surveying is essential.

audit.ageGap: A4 node; prerequisites from A3.

effectsProposed.why: A protected, buried supply keeps city water clean and secure, under siege too.

audit.rationale: Correct AND. Deliberate leaf; infra.aqueduct is OR with channel and arcade, so the node also carries a health effect.

audit.name: Aqueduct channel

prereqAssessment.why: A gravity channel over distance needs a measured fall.
The channel is lined and bridged in stone (Jerwan).

audit.ageGap: A4 node; prerequisites from A2, A3.

effectsProposed.why: Water piped into the city supports denser urban households.

audit.rationale: Correct AND. Feeds aqueduct_arcade.

audit.name: True arch

prereqAssessment.why: The first voussoir arches are Mesopotamian mudbrick.
Laying out the curve and the centring needs measured geometry; marginal but defensible.

audit.ageGap: A3 node; prerequisites from A2, A3.

effectsProposed.why: Arches and vaults roof rooms without long timber beams, which timber-poor plains lacked.

audit.rationale: Keep both atoms. surveying is the weaker atom, but replacing it would add an edge without evidence.

audit.name: Beam press

prereqAssessment.why: The beam press is a better oil press.
Press beds, weights and anchor stones are cut and set stone.

audit.ageGap: A4 node; prerequisites from A2. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Lever pressure extracts more oil from the same olive crop, so each grower's labour yields more.

audit.rationale: Correct AND. Deliberate leaf; oil export volumes are its game role.

audit.name: Water screw

prereqAssessment.why: The screw is the Archimedean helix applied to lifting.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A5.
audit.crossTree: Dependent screw_propeller (naval) is a sound downstream link.

effectsProposed.why: Screws drained Roman mines (Rio Tinto), so miners worked deeper ore.

audit.rationale: Correct, single causal prerequisite.

audit.name: Water-lifting wheel

prereqAssessment.why: A bucket wheel is a wheel on an axle.
The noria lifts from a channel or river into an irrigation system.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A2. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Lifted water irrigates fields above river level, so the irrigated share of arable land rises.

audit.costConcern: 2,960 is high against water_screw 1,760 for a similar lifting device; flag only.
audit.rationale: Correct AND. Deliberate leaf.

audit.name: Gear trains

prereqAssessment.why: Gear theory and calculation rest on Hellenistic mechanics.
Bronze gear blanks are cast; the Antikythera gears are cut bronze sheet and castings.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A3, A5.

effectsProposed.why: Geared instruments compute astronomical cycles, the start of the scientific-instrument tradition.

audit.costConcern: 5,910 is about twice the A5 lane peers (2,960-3,520); flag for calibration.
audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Vault and dome
audit.prereq: arch AND (concrete_pozzolan OR fired_brick OR ashlar_masonry)

prereqAssessment.why: Vaults and domes are arches extended or rotated.
Roman concrete vaults; alternative route, OR is right.
Brick vaults (Byzantine, Sasanian); alternative route.
Cut-stone vaults; alternative route.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A3, A5.

effectsProposed.why: Masonry and concrete roofs replace timber roofs that rot and burn.

audit.rationale: arch AND (any vaulting material) is the right shape.

audit.name: Stone arch bridge

prereqAssessment.why: A stone bridge is a chain of arches.
Roman bridge piers in concrete; alternative.
Cut-stone voussoirs; alternative.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A3, A5.

effectsProposed.why: Permanent river crossings remove fords and ferries, so overland travel is faster.

audit.rationale: Correct AND/OR. Deliberate leaf; its value is the live bridge.

audit.name: Arcaded aqueduct

prereqAssessment.why: The arcade carries the gravity channel.
Arcades are tiers of arches.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A3, A4.

effectsProposed.why: Abundant piped water for fountains and baths lowers urban disease.

audit.rationale: Correct AND. Deliberate leaf.

audit.name: Sericulture

prereqAssessment.why: Silk is a weaving fibre; a loom is needed.
Mulberry cultivation is tree-crop husbandry.

audit.ageGap: A3 node; prerequisites from A2.

effectsProposed.why: Silk is the archetypal high-value long-distance good, so trade networks close price gaps faster.

audit.costConcern: 620 is low for A3 (peers 1,760-2,960); flag for the integrator, no change proposed here.
audit.rationale: Correct AND. The node is the root of the figured-silk branch (drawloom).

audit.name: Fulling mill

prereqAssessment.why: Fulling stocks are cam-driven water hammers.
There must be woven woollen cloth to full.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A2, A5.
audit.rationale: Correct AND. The live building is the node's effect.

audit.name: Spinning wheel

prereqAssessment.why: The wheel drives a spindle.
A wheel on an axle, belt-driven.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A2. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Thread three times faster makes cloth cheaper, easing the Comfort need households feel.

audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Horizontal treadle loom

prereqAssessment.why: The treadle loom develops the upright loom.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A2. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Professional weaving becomes a trade that household spinners can rise into.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Roller cotton gin

prereqAssessment.why: Rollers turned by a crank wheel.
There must be cotton to gin.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A2. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Ginned lint is compact and ready to spin, so raw cotton stocks reach market faster.

audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Crank and connecting rod

prereqAssessment.why: Mill gear trains feed the crank.
Water power drives the first crank-and-rod sawmills (Hierapolis).

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A5.

effectsProposed.why: Powered saws and pumps raise timber and mining output per worker.

audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Verge escapement

prereqAssessment.why: A clock is a gear train.
The regulated timekeeping tradition the escapement mechanises.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A3, A5.

effectsProposed.why: Accurate clocks serve astronomy and found the precision-instrument craft.

audit.costConcern: 7,030 is the most expensive A6 node in the lane; flag for calibration.
audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Pound lock

prereqAssessment.why: Locks are built on dug canals.
Mitre and guillotine lock gates are framed timber.

audit.ageGap: A6 node; prerequisites from A2. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Locks let boats climb gradients, so canal and river haulage gets cheaper.

audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Type founding

prereqAssessment.why: Type is cast in a closed hand mould.

audit.ageGap: A7 node; prerequisites from A3. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change. Single A3 prerequisite for an A7 node: a four-Age gap, accepted.

effectsProposed.why: Cheap uniform type makes broadsheets, statutes and catechisms cheap to set.

audit.costConcern: 8,360 is high against canal_navigation 5,910; flag only.
audit.rationale: Keep. The A3-to-A7 gap is large, but nothing between them is causally required (punch-cutting is goldsmith work, outside the tree).

audit.name: Navigation canal

prereqAssessment.why: Summit-level freight canals need flights of locks.
Route and summit levels are surveyed.

audit.ageGap: A7 node; prerequisites from A3, A6.

effectsProposed.why: Bulk freight by canal costs about a quarter of road haulage.

audit.rationale: Correct AND. Deliberate leaf; the live canal is its main effect.

audit.name: Precision cylinder boring

prereqAssessment.why: Wilkinson's boring mill was a cannon-boring machine.
The boring bar was water-driven.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A5, A7.

effectsProposed.why: Sealed cylinders made Watt engines efficient mine pumps, so miners work deeper.

audit.costConcern: 33,450 is about 4x the A8 industry median (~8,360); flag for calibration.
audit.rationale: Correct AND (cross-lane to military).

audit.name: Slide-rest screw-cutting lathe

prereqAssessment.why: Heavy precision boring precedes the slide rest.
Clockmakers' screw-cutting lathes are the other ancestor.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A6, A8.

effectsProposed.why: Machined, standard-threaded iron parts make implements that wear less and can be repaired.

audit.costConcern: 33,450 is an outlier in A8 industry; flag.
audit.rationale: Correct AND. Its only entity (inst.standard_threads) is not live, so it carries an operand effect.

audit.name: Interchangeable parts

prereqAssessment.why: Precision screw-cutting and turning.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A8.

effectsProposed.why: Gauge-made implements with replaceable parts give equipped farmers better tools.

audit.rationale: Add milling_machine: the Harpers Ferry and Springfield achievement (Hall 1820s, North) depended on milling, not only turning. Milling (~1,818) predates the node (~1,820).

audit.name: Milling machine

prereqAssessment.why: Lead-screw feeds and precise slides.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A8.

effectsProposed.why: Machine shops need machinists and toolmakers, enlarging the skilled class.

audit.rationale: Correct. Gains interchangeable_parts as a dependent under the proposal.

audit.name: Flying shuttle

prereqAssessment.why: Kay's shuttle runs on a broadloom with a batten.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A5. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Doubled weaver output raised handloom earnings for a generation, a route up for craft households.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Spinning jenny

prereqAssessment.why: The jenny multiplies the spindles of the wheel.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A6. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Eight spindles per spinner make yarn and cloth cheap, easing the Comfort need.

audit.rationale: Correct.

audit.name: Water frame

prereqAssessment.why: Roller spinning develops wheel spinning.
The frame is water-powered.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A5, A6. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Mill employment draws rural families to factory villages such as Cromford.

audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Spinning mule

prereqAssessment.why: Carriage spinning from the jenny.
Drafting rollers from the frame.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A8.
audit.crossTree: Civic dependents: labour_unions. Dependent labour_unions is a civic.

effectsProposed.why: Fine mule yarn competes with Indian cloth, so cotton goods flow between markets.

audit.rationale: Correct AND (Crompton combined the two).

audit.name: Power loom

prereqAssessment.why: Mechanised picking extends the flying shuttle.
Power source; OR is right.
Power source; OR is right.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A5, A8.
audit.crossTree: Civic dependents: factory_inspection, labour_unions. Dependents factory_inspection and labour_unions are civics.

effectsProposed.why: Mill-woven cloth at scale makes clothing cheap for households.

audit.rationale: Correct AND/OR.

audit.name: Saw gin

prereqAssessment.why: The saw gin develops roller ginning.
The saw teeth are wire hooks or toothed discs.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A6. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: Upland cotton cleaned 50x faster: the ginning bottleneck no longer holds stock back from market.

audit.rationale: Correct AND. Deliberate leaf.

audit.name: Jacquard loom

prereqAssessment.why: The Jacquard head automates the drawloom's figure harness.
The pattern is punched into card.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A5. Nearest prerequisite is two or more Ages earlier; noted, not a reason to change.

effectsProposed.why: A stored, punched-card program is the direct ancestor of tabulation.

audit.rationale: Correct AND (cross-lane to communication).

audit.name: Reinforced concrete

prereqAssessment.why: Reinforced concrete is Portland-cement concrete.
Cheap mild-steel bar made reinforcement practical (Hennebique).

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A8.

effectsProposed.why: Fireproof concrete frames and floors outlast timber and brick.

audit.costConcern: 33,450 is high for A8 construction; flag.
audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Steel-frame skyscraper

prereqAssessment.why: The metal skeleton frame.
Steel beams (Home Insurance Building upper floors).
Electric lifts made tall buildings usable beyond ~10 storeys (1889 onward).

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A8. Currently A9 with only A8 prerequisites; proposed A8.
audit.crossTree: Civic dependents: zoning. Dependent zoning is an A9 civic; moving to A8 keeps it valid.

effectsProposed.why: Vertical cities: far more households per plot; a landmark node.

audit.costConcern: 66,910 is the most expensive node in the group; at A8 it needs recalibration with its new cohort.
audit.rationale: Move to A8: emerged 1885 sits inside the Industrial window (~1750-1914), the Chicago school is a pre-1914 phenomenon, and all three prerequisites are A8. A9 placement delays the unlock by an entire Age with no causal reason.

audit.name: Numerical control and robotics

prereqAssessment.why: Programs come from a computer.
The first NC machine was a milling machine (MIT 1952).

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A8, A9.

effectsProposed.why: Flexible automation shifts labour from machining to programming and maintenance, enlarging specialist classes.

audit.costConcern: 47,310 is high against desalination 16,730 and additive 11,830; flag.
audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Desalination

prereqAssessment.why: Pumps and plants need grid power.
Flash distillation route; OR is right.
Polymer membranes for reverse osmosis; OR is right.

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A5, A8, A9.
audit.rationale: Correct AND/OR. Deliberate leaf; the live plant is its effect.

audit.name: Additive manufacturing

prereqAssessment.why: Computer-controlled positioning.
First printers built in photopolymer.

audit.ageGap: A9 node; prerequisites from A9.

effectsProposed.why: Spare parts printed on demand keep tools and machines in service.

audit.rationale: Correct AND. Deliberate leaf.

audit.name: Ashlar (dressed-stone) masonry

prereqAssessment.why: Ashlar refines fitted stone construction.
Dressing blocks needs metal chisels and saws (with abrasive sand) — copper tools at Saqqara.

audit.ageGap: A3 node; prerequisites from A2.

effectsProposed.why: Dressed-stone footings and walls outlast earth, so buildings stand longer.

audit.rationale: Correct AND; hub for lighthouse, bridges, vaults and fortification.

audit.name: Pattern loom (drawloom)

prereqAssessment.why: The pattern loom was built for figured silks (jin).
The figure harness is mounted on a treadle loom.

audit.ageGap: A5 node; prerequisites from A3, A5.

effectsProposed.why: Figured weaving needs master weavers and drawboys, enlarging the skilled class.

audit.rationale: Correct AND.

audit.name: Sanitary engineering

prereqAssessment.why: Steam pumping drives water supply and sewage lifting.
Brick egg-section sewers.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A3, A8.

effectsProposed.why: Water-carriage sewerage and filtered supply cut waterborne disease sharply; a landmark node.

audit.rationale: Correct AND. Deliberate leaf.

audit.name: Structural iron

prereqAssessment.why: Coke smelting gave the cheap iron for the Iron Bridge and iron-framed mills.

audit.ageGap: A8 node; prerequisites from A7.

effectsProposed.why: Iron girder bridges span rivers and gorges, so roads can run further.

audit.rationale: Correct single prerequisite.

newNodes.name: Masonry dam and reservoir
newNodes.emerged: ~3,000 BCE Jawa (Jordan) dams and reservoirs; ~2,600 BCE Sadd el-Kafara (Egypt); ~2,500 BCE Dholavira reservoirs (Indus)
newNodes.prereqRationale: A dam is fitted stone and earth fill across a wadi (stone_dry); impounded water is only worth holding once fields are fed by channels (irrigation_canal). Both are A2 and centuries older than Jawa.
newNodes.desc: Walls of stone and earth across a valley hold back seasonal runoff, so channels can water the fields through a dry year.
newNodes.distinctFrom: irrigation_canal leads water already flowing; this stores it across seasons. hydroelectric (A9) is a power dam, not water storage for farming.

newNodes.name: Multi-storey apartment block
newNodes.emerged: ~218 BCE Rome (three-storey insulae noted by Livy); ~100 CE Ostia brick-faced concrete blocks of four to five storeys
newNodes.prereqRationale: Insulae stand on brick-faced pozzolan concrete walls; concrete (~300 BCE) and fired brick (~2,900 BCE) both predate the first recorded blocks.
newNodes.desc: Brick-faced concrete walls carry several floors of rented flats over street shops, packing many households onto one plot.
newNodes.distinctFrom: timber_frame houses one large household under one roof; this stacks many households vertically. The civic building_regulation (A5) regulates such blocks; this is the building technique itself.

newNodes.name: Balloon framing
newNodes.emerged: 1832 CE Chicago (George W. Snow); 1833 CE St Mary's Church, Chicago
newNodes.prereqRationale: It is light timber framing (timber_frame) made from standard sawn studs, which need powered crank-and-rod sawmills (crank_connecting_rod); both long predate 1832.
newNodes.desc: Light sawn studs nailed together replace heavy jointed timbers, so a small crew can raise a house in days.
newNodes.distinctFrom: timber_frame is jointed post-and-beam; this is a nailed frame of light sawn studs with no joinery, which cuts the labour per dwelling.

newNodes.name: Industrialised panel building
newNodes.emerged: 1953 CE Camus large-panel system (France); 1959 CE Soviet five-storey panel blocks
newNodes.prereqRationale: Factory-cast reinforced concrete panels (reinforced_concrete) are set in place by electric tower cranes (electric_motor); both are A8 and older than 1953.
newNodes.desc: Wall and floor panels are cast in factories and lifted into place by crane, so whole housing estates rise with little site labour.
newNodes.distinctFrom: reinforced_concrete is the material, poured on site; skyscraper is height and density. This is factory prefabrication of whole dwellings, which cuts labour per dwelling.

findings: Of 58 nodes, 22 had a live effect today (building./infra. unlocks). The other 36 had none, among them every mechanism and machine-tool node and 14 of the 17 textile nodes. Every node now carries a registry operand or a live unlock; in A8 industry, spinning_jenny and power_loom share society.grievanceRelief but differ in role, because power_loom also carries the textile_mill unlock.

Textiles (17 nodes, A2-A8) have no textile operand in the registry. Their effects therefore go through cloth's social and trade channels: Comfort/grievance, trade, specialist classes, migration to mills. A cloth-output operand (ProductionSystem fibre to cloth) would serve the lane better. Logged as a registry gap, not invented here.

Construction had no node at A6 or A7, and A9 would be empty once skyscraper moves to A8. insula (A5), balloon_frame (A8) and precast_housing (A9) fill the housing line. A7 stays empty on purpose: early-modern building advances were mostly fortification (military lane) and regulation (civics).
Infrastructure had no Bronze Age (A3) node between the Neolithic canals and the Iron Age water tunnels. reservoir_dam (Jawa, Sadd el-Kafara) fills it.

Three dependency changes are proposed. loom_warp_weighted drops timber_frame (not causal, and dated after the node). interchangeable_parts adds milling_machine. skyscraper moves from A9 to A8 (1885, all prerequisites are A8).

Cost outliers to calibrate: cylinder_boring and slide_rest_lathe (33,450 each, about 4x the A8 industry median), skyscraper 66,910 and numerical_control 47,310, gearing 5,910 (A5), escapement_verge 7,030 (A6), loom_warp_weighted 2,090 (A2). silk 620 is low for A3.

infra.aqueduct is an OR over three A4/A5 nodes, building.lighthouse is open via ashlar before stone_fortification, and building.textile_mill is OR over two A8 nodes. Only the first such node completed unlocks anything, so each also carries a distinct operand.

Civilization VI (base) and VII have no textile, fibre or machine-tool techs. Their tech trees jump from Pottery/Masonry to Machinery and Industrialization, so most of this lane is none-by-design there. Masonry, Irrigation, Engineering (aqueduct, bridge), Sanitation and Replaceable Parts/Robotics are the direct matches.
